title: US Stocks Week Ahead: PCE, GDP and Dell Earnings
summary: Thanksgiving week: US PCE and GDP land Wednesday, with Dell, Analog Devices and Deere earnings after the S&P 500 fell 8.61% last week.
body_markdown:
Markets will also look for clues about the Fed's December decision in Williams's remarks. His tone could move prices before Wednesday's data.


The GDP figure matters too. An economy growing too fast could keep the Fed's policy tight for longer.


Weekly jobless claims give a quick read on the labor market. Claims that stay low point to a tight job market, which can also keep inflation pressure alive.


Tuesday's Consumer Confidence report shows how US consumers feel heading into the holiday shopping season. It will be read alongside last month's retail sales.


The Beige Book collects reports on economic conditions from the Fed's 12 districts. Markets often use it to gauge price and wage pressure on the ground.


For readers outside the US, the Wednesday data falls on Wednesday evening in Asia, at 8:30 p.m. in GMT+7 and 9:30 p.m. in GMT+8 time zones.


## This Week's Earnings Calendar


Third-quarter earnings season is nearly over, but several large companies are still due to report. Times below follow US market hours.


Here is when some of the week's larger companies report, with consensus EPS estimates from Zacks:


- [Analog Devices (ADI)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/adi/) : Tuesday, November 24, before the open. Consensus EPS of US$3.89 on revenue of US$4.32 billion. The market will read demand for chips used in industry, cars and data centers.
- Dell Technologies: Tuesday, November 24, after the close. Consensus EPS of US$6.63 on revenue of US$50.63 billion. The market will read AI server demand, storage pricing and guidance for the next quarter.
- [Deere (DE)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/de/) : Wednesday, November 25, before the open. Consensus EPS of US$4.07 on revenue of US$10.30 billion. The market will read its fiscal 2027 guidance and farm equipment demand.


Other reports scheduled this week:


- Monday, after the close:[Zoom (ZM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/zm/) and[Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/hpe/) .
- Tuesday, before the open:[Best Buy (BBY)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/bby/) and[Medtronic (MDT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mdt/) .
- Tuesday, after the close:[Workday (WDAY)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/wday/) ,[Autodesk (ADSK)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/adsk/) and[HP (HPQ)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/hpq/) .


Best Buy's report will be read alongside consumer spending ahead of Black Friday. Reports from Dell, Workday and Autodesk will show how companies are spending on technology and AI.


## Market Sentiment


Sentiment is fragile. According to FXEmpire,[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) beat earnings estimates and raised its 2028 revenue guidance, but that failed to restore confidence in AI stocks.


Investors are now questioning how data center construction will be financed and what returns the huge AI spending will bring.


On the macro side, FXEmpire noted that October retail sales in the control group rose 0.6%, above the 0.3% consensus. Strong consumer spending raises the risk that inflation stays high.


That mix leaves markets sensitive in both directions. A softer PCE reading could ease pressure, while a hot number could add volatility.


On the technical side, FXEmpire said all three major indexes closed below their 52-week moving averages. The same outlet named 6,900 as the level the S&P 500 needs to hold.


Trading volume tends to be thin in Thanksgiving week, especially in Friday's short session. That can make price moves sharper than usual.


A few things you can prepare before this short week starts:


- Note the Wednesday release time in your own time zone, because PCE, GDP and jobless claims come out together.
- Watch the earnings released after the close, because the market reaction shows up only in the next session.
- Remember that liquidity can thin out in Friday's shortened session.


Black Friday on November 27 also gives an early read on US holiday spending. With most of this week's events packed into Wednesday, you may want to set your plan and risk limits before that data lands.
